approved: Broadcasting Legislation Amendment (Primary Television Broadcasting Service) Bill 2015
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
The bill would let commercial and national free-to-air television channels choose whether to broadcast their main channel in standard definition or high definition.
It removes the current legal requirement that the primary service must be in standard definition, and makes related changes to anti-siphoning and satellite licence rules.
The bill follows a 2015 review that found 96% of households can already receive high definition content.
Allows free-to-air broadcasters to offer their primary service in either SD or HD.
Updates the anti-siphoning regime to keep existing rules when a primary service is broadcast in HD.
Makes minor amendments to section 41CA and Schedule 2 of the Broadcasting Services Act 1992 for satellite-licence services.
Commercial and national free-to-air broadcasters and their viewers.

The Broadcasting Legislation Amendment (Primary Television Broadcasting Service) Bill 2015 removes the requirement for free-to-air broadcasters to transmit their primary service only in standard definition, allowing them to choose either standard or high definition for channels including ABC1, SBS ONE, 7, Prime7, Nine, WIN, Ten and Southern Cross. The speaker noted that 96% of households have HD-capable equipment and that the change would enable events such as the AFL and NRL grand finals to be broadcast in high definition.

The opposition supported the Broadcasting Legislation Amendment (Primary Television Broadcasting Service) Bill 2015, which removes the restriction requiring commercial broadcasters Seven, Nine, Ten, ABC and SBS to broadcast their primary channel only in standard definition, allowing high-definition broadcasts instead. The speaker noted that over 96% of Australian households now have HD-capable televisions, and the change will enable major sporting events like AFL and NRL grand finals to be shown in HD.
